column2: Those who bow to the god Bhaskara, praised by Shakra and others, are freed from all sins and go to the Sun's world.
For a long time, Brahma, a desire to hear has arisen in us: tell us the hundred and eight names of the Sun that you told formerly.

Hear the hundred and eight names as I tell, the supreme secret of Bhaskara, Brahmins, which gives heaven and liberation.
brahmapuran:33:34	Om. Surya, Aryaman, Bhaga, Tvashta, Pusha, Arka, Savita, Ravi, Gabhastiman, Aja, Kala, Mrityu, Dhata, Prabhakara,
brahmapuran:33:35	Earth, Water, Fire, Space, Wind, the Supreme Refuge, Soma, Brihaspati, Shukra, Budha, Angaraka,
brahmapuran:33:36	Indra, Vivasvan, Diptamshu, Shuchi, Shauri, Shanaishchara, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Skanda, Vaishravana, Yama,
brahmapuran:33:37	Vaidyuta, Jatharagni, Aindhana, Lord of Lights, Dharmadhvaja, Vedakarta, Vedanga, Vedavahana,
brahmapuran:33:38	Krita, Treta, Dvapara, Kali, the refuge of all immortals, Kala, Kashtha, Muhurta, Kshapa, Yama, Kshana,
brahmapuran:33:39	Maker of the year, Ashvattha, Kalachakra, Vibhavasu, Purusha, Eternal, Yogi, Manifest-Unmanifest, Sanatana,
brahmapuran:33:40	Overseer of Time, Overseer of creatures, Vishvakarma, Dispeller of darkness, Varuna, Sagara, Amsha, Jimuta, Jivana, Foe-slayer,
brahmapuran:33:41	Refuge of beings, Lord of beings, Bowed to by all worlds, Creator, Samvartaka, Fire, Beginning of all, Free from greed,
brahmapuran:33:42	Ananta, Kapila, Bhanu, Giver of desires, Facing all sides, Jaya, Vishala, Boon-giver, Served by all beings,
brahmapuran:33:43	Mind, Suparna, Origin of beings, Swift-moving, Sustainer of life, Dhanvantari, Dhumaketu, Primal God, Aditi's son,
brahmapuran:33:44	Twelvefold Self, Ravi, Daksha, Father, Mother, Grandfather, Door of heaven, Door of creatures, Door of liberation, Trivishtapa,
brahmapuran:33:45	Maker of bodies, Tranquil-souled, Universal Self, Facing all sides, Self of the moving and unmoving, Subtle Self, Maitreya, Compassionate.
brahmapuran:33:46	This lovely hundred and eight names of the praiseworthy Sun of immeasurable brilliance has been told by me, best of Brahmins.
brahmapuran:33:47	Served by hosts of gods, ancestors and Yakshas, worshipped by Asuras, the moon and Siddhas, bright as excellent gold and fire — I bow to Bhaskara for my welfare."
The man who, well composed, recites this at sunrise gains wife and sons, heaps of wealth and jewels, remembrance of past births, and attains supreme memory and intelligence.
The man who with pure mind and composure recites this hymn of the best of gods is freed from the ocean of the wildfire of grief and obtains the desires he wishes in mind.
When Daksha, the householder, lord of sacrifices, performed that sacrifice together with the deities,
then, goddess Sati — in the Vaivasvata interval — the king of mountains begot the goddess Uma on Mena.
That goddess Sati was earlier, and afterwards became Uma; she is Bhava's companion in vows, and Bhava is not freed from her.
As long as the lord wishes to continue in the manvantaras here, the goddess is devoted, like Aditi to Marichi's son Kashyapa,
Shri with Narayana, Shachi with Maghavan, Kirti with Vishnu, Usha with the Sun, and Arundhati with Vasishtha.
These goddesses never leave their husbands in any way. Thus Daksha, son of Prachetas, was born in the Chakshusha interval,
grandson of Prachinabarhis and son of the Prachetases; from the ten Prachetases again, king, on Marisha,
he was born through Rudra's curse, the second time, so we have heard. Bhrigu and the others were all born as great sages.
In the first Treta yuga, formerly, in the sacrifice of the great god of Manu Vaivasvata, bearing the Varuni form,
there was this remorse for the two of them, carried into another birth, of Daksha the Prajapati and the wise Tryambaka.

Therefore one should never nurse resentment toward the great; even one gone to another birth is affected by the good and bad that is to come. Fame brings no prosperity to a creature in that case; one who knows should not do that.

How, lord, did she, Daksha's daughter Sati, formerly, in anger, abandon her body and was born again in the house of the king of mountains?
brahmapuran:34:52	In the other body, how was there her former body, and how the union with Bhava and the dialogue between them?
brahmapuran:34:53	How did the svayamvara occur in that great birth, and the marriage, lord of the world, full of all wonders?
brahmapuran:34:54	Brahma, you ought to tell all that in detail now; we wish to hear the holy, very charming story.

Hear, tigers among sages, the sin-destroying, holy story of Uma and Shankara, which grants the fruit of all desires.
brahmapuran:34:56	Once Himavan asked Kashyapa, best of two-footed beings, who had come from his own house, about conduct that creates fame in the world and is beneficial:
brahmapuran:34:57	'By what do worlds become imperishable, and the highest fame, sage, and likewise being worthy of honour among the good? Tell me that.'
brahmapuran:34:58	'Mighty-armed one, all this is obtained by offspring. Fame comes to me through offspring, with Brahma and the sages.'
brahmapuran:34:59	'Do you not see, king of mountains, since you ask me? I shall tell what I saw formerly, mountain.
brahmapuran:34:60	Going to Varanasi I saw in the sky a vehicle, very new, divine, incomparable, of great splendour.
brahmapuran:34:61	Below it, in a pit, I heard a cry of distress. Knowing that by austerity, I stood there, invisible.
brahmapuran:34:62	Then, king of mountains, a Brahmin came there, observing restraints, pure, his self purified by bathing at holy places, established in supreme austerity.
brahmapuran:34:63	Then the Brahmin, going along, frightened by a tiger, entered that place, mountain, where the pit was.
brahmapuran:34:64	In the pit he saw sages hanging from a clump of vīraṇa grass, distressed, and in pain he asked them:
brahmapuran:34:65	Who are you hanging from the vīraṇa clump, face downward, suffering? How will you, sinless ones, be liberated?"

We are your forefathers, with grandfathers and great-grandfathers, of you who have gained merit; we are tormented by your evil act.
brahmapuran:34:67	This is hell, fortunate one, standing in the form of a pit; you too are the vīraṇa clump, and we hang on you.
brahmapuran:34:68	As long as you live, Brahmin, so long do we stay; when you die we, of sinful mind, shall go to hell.
brahmapuran:34:69	If, having married, you beget an excellent child, by that we shall be freed from sin.
brahmapuran:34:70	Not by other austerity, son, nor by the fruit of holy places; do this, greatly wise one, and save your ancestors from fear.
He, promising "So be it," propitiated the bull-bannered Lord and, lifting his ancestors out of the pit, made them leaders of Shiva's hosts.
One, beloved of Rudra himself, named Suvesha, esteemed and mighty, became a leader of Rudra's hosts.
Therefore, king of mountains, practise severe austerity and beget a highly virtuous offspring, a daughter of excellent complexion."
Thus told by the sage, the king of mountains, firm in restraint, performed incomparable austerity, by which I was pleased.
Then I rose before him and said, "I am the giver of boons. Speak, king of mountains, I am pleased with this austerity, of good vows."
Revered one, I want a son adorned with all virtues; grant me such a boon, lord, if you are pleased with me.
Hearing that word of the king of mountains, Brahmins, I then gave him the boon desired in mind:

You will have a daughter, king of mountains, by this austerity, good one, by whose power you will gain good fame everywhere,
brahmapuran:34:79	worshipped by all the gods, surrounded by crores of holy places, and purifying, by merit, even the gods on all sides.
brahmapuran:34:80	She will be your eldest, and others here too, auspicious one.
In time the king of mountains begot on Mena Aparna, Ekaparna and Ekapatala.
Eating only a banyan leaf, one (Ekaparna), and a patala leaf, Ekapatala; Aparna practised austerity without a home.
For a hundred thousand years, austerity hard for gods and Danavas; Ekaparna lived on one leaf as food.
And Ekapatala lived on a single patala; when a thousand years were complete, the two took food.
But Aparna took no food; her mother, distressed with maternal affection, said to her, "U mā" (O don't!), forbidding her.
Thus addressed by her mother, the goddess who practised austerity hard to practise became famed in the worlds by that very name (Uma) and worshipped by the gods.
This triple group of maidens, the world of moving and unmoving, their austerity's account will last as long as the earth endures.
All three, with austerity as their bodies, took to yoga; all were fortunate and had stable youth.
They are mothers of the world and celibate, and always favour the worlds by their own austerity.
Uma, the eldest and best of them, of fair complexion, endowed with the power of great yoga, approached Mahadeva.
Ushana's son Dattaka was the delight of Bhrigu's family; Ekaparna bore a son, Devala, to him.
The third of those maidens, Ekapatala, bore a son to Alarka's son, Jaigishavya, whom she approached.
Her two sons, Shankha and Likhita, are remembered as not born from a womb. Uma, the fair-complexioned, is she who was told to you by me.
Then, seeing the whole three worlds heated by her austerity's yoga, I said to her:

Goddess, why will you torment the worlds with austerity, auspicious one? All this was created by you; do not destroy it.
brahmapuran:34:96	You support all these worlds by your own brilliance; tell us, mother of the world, what you wish for now.
For whose sake this austerity is practised by me, Grandfather — you know that yourself; so why ask again?
Then I said to her, "He for whose sake you practise austerity, auspicious one, will himself come here and choose you.
Sharva alone is the best husband, lord of the lords of all worlds, whose servants we always are, obedient, auspicious one.
That god of gods, the Supreme Lord, self-born, will come near you, goddess — of noble form, of terrible and other forms, whose form is equal to nothing of anyone.

The great Lord, dwelling in the mountain world, lord of the moving and unmoving, the first, immeasurable, who stands as if in a terrifying form without the moon, though with a brilliance like Indra's."
Longing for Bhava, the great Lord, master of the worlds, she was then dejected and did not shine, like night without the moon.
Then the daughter of the mountain heard the cry of a distressed boy at a lake full of water near the hermitage.
The god of gods, Shiva himself, assuming the form of a boy, for the sake of sport became seized by a crocodile in the middle of the lake.
Resorting to yoga-maya, the cause of the world's origin, he made that form in the middle of the lake and spoke thus:
Let someone save me! he said, his mind seized by the crocodile. "Alas, I am a mere boy, my wishes unfulfilled.
I go to death in the mouth of this evil crocodile. I do not grieve for my own body, seized by the crocodile, in great pain;
I grieve for my father and my austere mother, who, hearing that I am caught by the crocodile and have met death, will eagerly
give up their lives, having a beloved only son. Alas, how sad, that I, a boy not yet married, held inside the crocodile, shall go to death."
Hearing that cry of the distressed Brahmin, the beautiful goddess rose and set out to where that Brahmin was.
The moon-faced one saw a boy of lovely form, caught in the mouth of the crocodile, standing trembling.
The excellent glorious crocodile too, seeing the goddess approach, quickly went with him to the middle of the lake.
Being dragged, he, full of brilliance, made a cry of distress. Then the goddess, pained, seeing the boy seized by the crocodile, said:
King of crocodiles, great being, release this only son, great-fanged, of dreadful valour, quickly.

Goddess, whoever first comes to me on the sixth day is my food, ordained long ago by the creators of the world.
brahmapuran:35:45	He is mine, fortunate one, on the sixth day, daughter of the mountain king, sent surely by Brahma; I shall not release him in any way.
By the supreme austerity practised by me on the peak of the Himalaya, release this boy, king of crocodiles; salutation to you.
Do not waste your austerity greatly for a boy, goddess of fair face; do as I say, best one, and thus he will gain release.
Lord of crocodiles, say quickly what is not censured by the good; that will be done, no doubt, since Brahmins are dear to me.
Whatever small, excellent austerity has been done by you, give me all of it at once; then he will gain release.
Great crocodile, whatever merit I have made from birth onward, all that I have given you; release the boy, great crocodile.
Then the crocodile, adorned by that austerity, blazed like the midday sun, hard to look at, and spoke thus, with a pleased heart, to the goddess who supports the world:

Goddess, why do you do this? Having considered well, great-vowed one: acquiring austerity is painful, and giving it up is not praised.
brahmapuran:35:53	Take back your austerity and this boy, slender-waisted one; I am pleased with your devotion to a Brahmin, so I give you a boon. Thus addressed by the crocodile, the great-vowed one said:

Crocodile, a Brahmin must be protected diligently even by my body; austerity can be obtained again by me, a Brahmin cannot be obtained again.
brahmapuran:35:55	Having considered well, great crocodile, the release of the boy has been done; austerity is not better than Brahmins, Brahmins are held better by me.
brahmapuran:35:56	Having given, I do not take back, king of crocodiles; it has been ordained for you; no man ever takes back what has been given.
brahmapuran:35:57	This has been given by me to you and I do not take it back; let this stay with you, and let this boy be released.
Thus addressed, he praised her, released the boy, bowed to the goddess, and disappeared on the spot, shining like the sun.
The boy too, released by the crocodile on the lake's shore, vanished there like a treasure obtained in a dream.
Thinking her austerity diminished, the goddess, daughter of the Himalaya, firm in restraint, began again to perform austerity.
Knowing her desire to perform austerity again, Shankara himself, Brahmins, said these words: "Do not perform austerity.
This austerity, goddess of great vows, was given to me by you; therefore it will become imperishable for you, a thousandfold."
Having obtained that boon of imperishable supreme austerity, the goddess stood pleased and glad, awaiting her svayamvara.
The man who always recites this account of Shambhu's child-like deeds, having attained the separation of the body, becomes pure, and equal to Kumara, as Ganesha.
Mounting, the lord of all wealth, the king of kings, came hurriedly, gladdening all the lords of gods and Asuras by his radiance and attire, lovely in form.
The Moon came, mounting a vehicle of great jewels shining in various forms, with dark-blue body, in strange attire, his whole body garlanded with fragrant garlands.
The mace-bearer (Vishnu), mounting Garuda, who was like a mountain, came hurriedly; then the two Ashvins, best of physicians, quickly mounted a single vehicle,
charming, blazing, of lovely attire, the two excellent gods, heroic, arrived; the thousand-headed Naga, bearing then a flaming fire-colour, with the brilliance of fire and sun,
the great-souled one, along with other serpents, mounted a vehicle and came; the sons of Diti and the great Asuras, with the radiance of fire, sun, Shakra and wind,
having prepared attire befitting the occasion, came as a band before the gods; the king of Gandharvas too, handsome, with divine armlets, moving in a divine vehicle,
together with hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases, came there by Indra's command; and other gods from heaven then, each with lovely adopted attire,
came mounted on the backs of vehicles, with Gandharvas, Yakshas, serpents and Kinnaras; and the lord of Shachi shone there amid the gods, with a form seeming more than kingly,
delighted by the might and power of command, adorned that svayamvara. The cause of the three worlds, the mother of the world's origin, mother of them with gods and Asuras,
and wife of Shambhu, the wise Purusha, sung in the Purana as the supreme Prakriti, came to the Himalaya's house, through Daksha's anger, for the gods' sake.
Standing on the back of a vehicle inlaid with jewels and gold, her limbs fanned by waving chauris, the goddess took a garland of flowers of all seasons, very fragrant, and set forth boldly.
When the goddess, holding the garland, stood in the assembly of gods, and the gods led by Shakra had come to the svayamvara,
Shambhu, wishing to test the goddess, became a five-crested child and suddenly lay asleep in her lap, the lord.
Then the goddess saw him, the five-crested child, and, knowing him by meditation, took him up with love.
Then she, of pure intention, having got her desired good husband, turned back and stood, holding that lord in her heart.
Then the gods, seeing the child on the goddess's lap, consulted, "Who is this here?" and cried out, greatly bewildered.
The slayer of Vritra, raising his arm, took up the thunderbolt against him; that arm of his stood raised just as it was.
Paralysed by the god of gods Shambhu in child form, Vritra's slayer could not throw the thunderbolt nor move.
Then the mighty god Bhaga, the Aditya, son of Kashyapa, bewildered, raised a blazing weapon wishing to strike.
The Lord paralysed his arm too in the same way, and likewise paralysed his strength, brilliance and yoga.
Vishnu, shaking his head, looked at Shankara. Then, while the gods stood thus, angry,
I, greatly alarmed, took to meditation with reverence and understood the lord of gods seated on Uma's lap.
Knowing the Supreme Lord, I quickly rose and reverently bowed to Shambhu's feet and praised him, Brahmins:
with Puranas, Sama chants, holy-named and secret names: "You are unborn, ageless God, Creator, all-pervading, the higher and the lower,
the Pradhana, the Purusha that you are, Brahman to be meditated, the Imperishable, the Immortal, Supreme Self, Lord, the cause, the Great.
Creator of Brahma, maker of Prakriti, maker of all, beyond Prakriti; and this goddess Prakriti is always the cause of your creation.
Assuming the form of a wife she has come as the cause of the world. Salutation to you, Mahadeva, together with the goddess.
By your grace, lord of gods, and by your command, creatures were created by me; these gods and others, deluded by your yoga-maya.
Show grace to them, that they may be as before." Thus, Brahmins, I informed the Supreme Lord.
And to those paralysed gods I then said this: "Foolish gods all, you do not know this is Shankara.
Go quickly for refuge to this very Maheshvara, together with me, the lord of gods, the imperishable Supreme Self."
Then all of them, the dwellers in heaven, paralysed as they were, bowed to Sharva in mind, with a heart purified by devotion.
Then the god of gods, Maheshvara, became pleased with them and at once restored the gods' bodies as before.
Then, when all the gods' hindrance had been thus removed, the lord of gods took a supreme, wondrous three-eyed form.
Struck down by his brilliance, they all shut their eyes; he gave them supreme sight, the power of vision to see his form.
